reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the webinar promotes joining OneCoin through a signup link and purchasing packages costing up to 5,000 euros in exchange for tokens and related cryptocurrency opportunities. It presents possible bonuses of 18,000 euros per week tied to recruiting successive levels of participants, while projected prices and future exchange access are promotional predictions rather than established outcomes. The visible disclaimer qualifies the figures as predictions, and the records do not establish actual trading, payouts, or realized losses.

So only thirty people you'd still be making six hundred and twenty euros per week It's not monthly this weekly in matching bonus

opening.argument: The presentation repeatedly frames participation as something to investigate rather than accept blindly. It asks whether an opportunity is real, legal, simple, and has a genuine market, and explicitly warns that dependence on network members would be a red flag. Its earnings discussion also qualifies outcomes by package, while the projected price chart is expressly based on predictions and dependent on participant effort. That combination is consistent with conditional promotion and disclosed uncertainty, not a representation that every viewer will receive a guaranteed return.

citations.quote: Too many people jump into different opportunities without checking things out.
if the only people who are able or willing to buy your product or service are members within the network or have to join the network to do so, then that's a red flag.
that doesn't necessarily mean they all earn 35,000 euros a week, because it depends on which package they have.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats conditional figures as if they were guarantees, but its own quotations show only that bonuses are calculated through levels and that one example could produce weekly income. The presentation qualifies the figures rather than concealing uncertainty: it says earnings depend on the package and displays a prediction disclaimer. A future projection, without proof of actual trading or payouts, does not by itself establish deceptive certainty.

citations.quote: that doesn't necessarily mean they all earn 35,000 euros a week, because it depends on which package they have.
18,000 Euros per week just in matching bonus alone is possible

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualifications do not neutralize the solicitation. The video still promotes paid packages, mining permissions, and multi-level bonuses, while presenting large possible earnings as an incentive. Saying an outcome is “possible” or package-dependent does not show that the underlying figures are reliable, that participants can withdraw funds, or that the projected price will be reached. The chart disclaimer concedes that the values are only predictions, not evidence of an established market.

opening.argument: The central format is an online educational presentation explaining cryptocurrency concepts and the operation of a platform. The speaker calls OneAcademy the core activity, describes interactive videos, presentations, quizzes, and trading instruction, and explains how tokens are used within an internal exchange. The accompanying slide likewise labels the core activity as online education. Those are tutorial and operational-demonstration features; the material can be understood as explaining a business model and technology rather than documenting a completed financial outcome.

citations.quote: sell our online educational products all over Europe
the one academy, our core activity
interactive material like videos presentations and quizzes, how to make money with crypto currency, how to trade it.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the event educational does not answer what it teaches viewers to do. The presentation connects its education packages to tokens, mining permissions, internal trading, and member sales. The cited description of quizzes and videos identifies the format, but it does not establish that education is the primary value delivered or that the associated financial opportunity is merely illustrative.

citations.quote: each package gives you free tokens
They also give you the opportunity to practice what you are learning in the OneAcademy in trading on our trading platform, our internal exchange.
you can sell those tokens for a profit to other members

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational label is part of the sales structure, not a separate neutral lesson. The packages cost from 100 to 5,000 euros and supply tokens or mining permissions, so the presentation ties instruction to a paid opportunity. Explaining the mechanics does not establish legitimacy, independent educational value, or actual cryptocurrency activity; it can equally function as instruction for recruiting and purchasing into the scheme.

opening.argument: The offer is presented as the sale of online education products with package-specific contents and associated tokens, not as a demand for an unspecified deposit. The speaker expressly says the company sells online education, does not sell coins, and describes tokens as permissions connected to the educational program. The supplied evidence does not establish a guaranteed return, a completed payout, or a request for credentials. At most, it shows a commercial package and referral-based benefits whose real-world results remain unproven.

citations.quote: we sell education products online
we do not sell coins we do nor currency.
each package gives you free tokens
you can sell those tokens for a profit to other members

rebuttal.rebuttal: The ordinary-commerce framing omits the actual incentive structure. The presentation lists packages up to 5,000 euros, says tokens permit mining, and calculates matching bonuses through four generations. A conventional product description does not explain away income tied to recruiting successive participants. The absence of a proven payout cannot convert those specific recruitment and purchase mechanics into ordinary retail.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The package labels do not make the transaction ordinary commerce when the advertised value depends on mining permissions, internal token sales, and recruitment bonuses. The speaker says the company does not sell coins, but the same presentation says packages provide tokens and that tokens may be sold for profit to members. That is evidence of a paid entry structure tied to a member network, even if the record does not show a completed payout.
